signin.title: What’ll it be?
signin.lead: Use the passkey on this device, or your username and password.
signin.passwordSet: Password saved. Sign in with it.

errors.invalidToken: That link is no longer valid. Ask the printer owner for a fresh one.
errors.tokenExpired: That link expired. Ask the printer owner for another.
errors.suspended: That account has been suspended. Ask whoever owns the printer.
errors.other: That sign-in attempt did not go through.

form.refused: That username and password do not match. Try again.
form.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.

form.inviteOnly: Pretty Please Print is invite-only — there is no sign-up. If you have not been invited yet, or you have forgotten your password, ask whoever owns the printer.

account.passkeys: {count, plural, one {# passkey on this account} other {# passkeys on this account}}
account.docsHint: Every endpoint, and a console to call them from.

nudge.title: Tired of typing your password?
nudge.body: Save a passkey and this device signs you in with a fingerprint — nothing to remember, nothing to phish.

themes.glass: Glass — see-through panels over a colourful room
themes.auto: Follow the system — the diner by day, after hours in dark mode

slicer.help: Opens {slicer} on this machine. Needs the one-time helper — see the setup. Nothing happens if it is not installed — the download beside this works anywhere.

preferences.title: How you like it
preferences.lead: Your language, how the place looks, and the slicer named on the button of every ticket. Left to the house, each one follows the printer owner’s choice — today and when it changes.
preferences.languageHelp: Left to the house, your browser’s language comes first, if this app speaks it.
preferences.slicerHelp: Only the button’s name changes. The helper on your own machine decides which slicer opens.
preferences.refused: That is not on the menu. Pick from the list.

settingsDefaults.title: For everyone who has not chosen
settingsDefaults.lead: Each person can pick their own on their page; these are what everyone else gets, the sign-in page included.
settingsDefaults.languageHelp: For a browser that asks for no language this app speaks, or for none. A browser asking for English or French still gets it.
settingsDefaults.slicerHelp: The name on the slicer button of every ticket — “Open in your slicer” for another slicer. Only the label: the helper on each machine decides what opens.

setup.title: Before the doors open
setup.lead: Six short steps to get the counter ready. Each one can be skipped, and everything here can be changed later at Settings.
setup.leadAgain: The six steps a new instance starts with, to go through again. Everything here is also at Settings.
setup.reauthNote: Saving asks for your password or passkey again if you signed in more than five minutes ago, as it does at Settings.
setup.skipAll: Skip the rest of the setup
setup.skipAllHelp: It will not open by itself again. It stays at Settings, whenever you want it.
setup.doneAlready: This instance is past its first run; nothing here opens by itself any more.

toast.saved: Saved — in effect from the next request

account.lead: Your account is open: the link from the logs gave it a username and a password, and that is the way in that always works.
account.name: Name
account.hasPasskey: {count, plural, one {This account has a passkey. Signing in is a fingerprint or a face.} other {This account has # passkeys. Signing in is a fingerprint or a face.}}
account.passkeyWhy: One thing worth thirty seconds: save a passkey. It puts your fingerprint, face or device PIN where the password goes — nothing to remember, nothing to phish.
account.passkeyLater: Needs a browser that does passkeys, with JavaScript on. Not now? The account menu offers it whenever you like.

address.lead: Sign-in cookies, passkeys and every link in an e-mail are tied to one address: APP_URL, in .env.docker. This step only checks it — it stays in the environment.
address.match: They match: this is the address the app expects.
address.mismatch: They differ. Sign-in cookies are set for {app}, Better Auth refuses forms sent from anywhere else, and invitations and reset links point there — so from {seen}, signing in and passkeys fail, and links lead elsewhere. Open the app at {app}, or set APP_URL to the address people will use and restart the stack.
address.rpIdOk: Passkeys are bound to {rpId}, which covers {host}.
address.rpIdBad: Passkeys are bound to {rpId}, which does not cover {host}: browsers will refuse to make or use one. PASSKEY_RP_ID has to be {host} or a domain above it — and it is permanent once somebody has a passkey, so fix it before.

look.lead: For everyone who has not chosen on their own page, the sign-in page included. The same two defaults as at Settings, saved the same way.

mail.lead: Mail only ever delivers a link — an invitation, or a password reset. Without it the app shows you the link to hand over yourself, which works too.
mail.sendHelp: To your own address only, and at most {count} in {minutes} minutes.
mail.noneHow: To send mail, set one of SMTP_URL or RESEND_API_KEY in .env.docker, with MAIL_FROM for the address it comes from, then restart the stack:
mail.noneFine: Or leave it: running without mail is a supported way to run this app.

problem.noTransport: There is no transport to send through.
problem.tooMany: That makes {count} test messages in {minutes} minutes. Give it a moment before the next.
problem.refused: The transport refused the message. The app’s log says why.
problem.refusedCode: The transport refused the message ({code}). The app’s log says why.

slicer.lead: Every ticket has a button that opens its model in a slicer, through a small helper installed once on the computer with the printer. The button’s name first, then the helper.
slicer.platform: This browser says it runs on {os}.

os.other: a system the helper has no installer for

slicer.linux: On the computer with the slicer, from a checkout of the source:
slicer.windows: It needs Git for Windows. Open PowerShell in a checkout of the source — Shift + right-click in the folder, then “Open PowerShell window here” — and run:
slicer.windowsNote: No administrator rights: it installs under your own profile, and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass applies to this one run only.
slicer.macos: There is no installer for macOS: the link is registered by a small app you make once in Script Editor. The steps are in the guide:
slicer.other: Install it on the computer that has the slicer — a phone or a tablet cannot run it. The guide covers Linux, Windows and macOS.
slicer.conf: Then give it this instance’s address, in ~/.config/ppp/slicer.conf:

people.lead: Nobody gets in without an invitation. Send the first one from the guest list: by mail if mail is set up, or as a link you hand over yourself.
people.finish: Finish — take me to the pass
people.finishInvite: Finish and send the first invitation

revisit.title: First-run setup
revisit.body: The six steps a new instance starts with: the address, mail, the slicer helper and the rest.

passkey.done: Passkey saved. Next time, signing in is a fingerprint or a face — the password still works if you would rather.
passkey.failed: That did not complete. The account menu offers it again whenever you like.

board.lead: Ask for a change to Pretty Please Print, and follow it through the same stages a print goes through. {owner} sees each one and moves it along.
board.emptyHelp: The first idea goes on the board the moment you file it.

new.title: Ask for a feature
new.lead: Say what you are hoping for and why. {owner} sees it on the board and takes it from there.
new.descriptionPlaceholder: What you'd like, and what it would let you do.

detail.withdrawHelp: This removes it and its conversation. Only while nobody has started on it.

conversation.title: Talk it over
conversation.label: Add to the conversation
conversation.placeholderOwner: Ask a question, or say what you changed…

actions.declineHelp: This closes it. The requester is told.

not_found.title: That link means nothing to us
not_found.body: It may have been mistyped, or the invitation was withdrawn. Ask whoever owns the printer to send a fresh one.

expired.title: That invitation expired
expired.body: Invitations last a week. Ask for another and it will work straight away.

revoked.title: That invitation was withdrawn
revoked.body: Whoever sent it has since cancelled it. If that seems wrong, have a word with them.

already_accepted.title: That invitation has been used
already_accepted.body: The account already exists — sign in instead. Invitation links only work once, on purpose.

invite.title: {name} will print things for you
invite.lead: Upload an <mono>.stl</mono> or <mono>.3mf</mono>, say what you are hoping for, and it lands on the backlog as a story you can follow. Pick a name to go by, a username and a password, and you are in.
invite.notice: This link registers the account — there is no second email. You are signed in the moment it is created, and the next screen offers a passkey so you can skip the password on this device.

form.emailHelp: The invite is tied to this address and cannot be moved to another.
form.name: What should we call you?
form.nameHelp: Shown on your tickets and in the conversation.
form.passwordHelp: At least {min} characters. Length beats punctuation.

fields.usernameHelp: What you sign in with — letters, digits, - and _

setPassword.spentBody: Set-password links work once and expire quickly. Ask whoever owns the printer for another — it takes them a moment.
setPassword.leadSetUp: Nobody invited this account, so it has no username yet. Pick one, and a password to go with it.
setPassword.leadPick: This link sets a password and nothing else — you will sign in with it on the next screen. Anything you were signed in on with the old one is signed out.
setPassword.notice: Did not ask for this? Have a word with whoever runs the printer before you use it.

form.passwordHelp: At least {min} characters, and not a breached one.

reauth.title: Is that still you?
reauth.lead: You are about to change who can get in, or how the app behaves for everyone. A password or a passkey confirms it is you at the keyboard and not a browser somebody left open.

form.passkeyRefused: That passkey was not accepted. Use your password instead.
form.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
form.refused: That password does not match. Try again.

welcome.title: Welcome, {name}
welcome.lead: One last thing worth thirty seconds: save a passkey. It puts your fingerprint, face or device PIN where the password goes, and unlike a password there is nothing to phish, reuse or forget.

prompt.unsupported: This browser does not do passkeys. Your username and password work everywhere, which is why they are the way in.
prompt.done: Passkey saved. Next time, signing in is a fingerprint or a face — no password to type. It still works if you would rather.
prompt.failed: That did not complete. You can always add one later.
prompt.notNow: Not now — keep typing my password

feature.requesterOnly: Only the person who asked for it can withdraw it.

alreadyStarted.InProgress: {ref} is already in progress — ask {owner} instead.

feature.reprioritiseRefused: Only the person who asked for it, or the printer owner, can reprioritise it.

endOfLine.Declined: Declined is the end of the line.

cannotDecline.Declined: Cannot decline a request that is already Declined.

feature.descriptionEmpty: Say what you are hoping for.
feature.commentLong: That is longer than a comment wants to be.

auth.usernameLong: A username can be at most {max} characters.
auth.usernameRule: A username is {min}–{max} characters: letters, digits, hyphen or underscore.

auth.failedMoment: That did not go through. Try again in a moment.

catalog.secondColour: Choose a valid second gradient colour.
catalog.materialName: Material names must be between 1 and 40 characters.
catalog.materialAtEnd: That material is already at the end of the list.
catalog.colourAtEnd: That colour is already at the end of the list.

senderName.nameOnly: Sender name: A name only — no quotes, angle brackets, backslashes or line breaks. The address stays in MAIL_FROM.

catalog.kicker: Admin · what is on the shelf
catalog.title: Materials & colours
catalog.lead: Offer only combinations you can actually print today. Use the arrows to set the order shown on the request form. Turning something off hides it temporarily; removing it deletes the catalog entry and its colours. Old tickets are unchanged either way.
catalog.noColours: No colours yet. This material will stay off the order form.

done.materialAdded: {name} added. Give it at least one colour to offer it.
done.materialRemoved: {name} and its colours were removed. Old tickets are unchanged.
done.colourRemoved: {name} was removed from {material}. Old tickets are unchanged.

catalogEdit.removeColorConfirm: Remove {name} from {material}? Old tickets will be kept.
catalogEdit.removeMaterialConfirm: Remove {name} and all of its colours? Old tickets will be kept.

prints.title: Prints by person
prints.lead: Pick one person or several to see everything they have uploaded, in any state — waiting, on the bed, finished or declined. Pick somebody again to take them out.
prints.nobody: Nobody picked yet. Choose somebody above.
prints.ticketsFrom: {count, plural, one {# ticket} other {# tickets}} from {whose}

benefits.title: What’s in it for you
benefits.lead: The tips people can offer when they ask for a print. Mark the ones you currently prefer — those are starred on the upload form so people know what you actually want. Retire one to take it off the list without touching past requests that offered it.
benefits.empty: No benefits on the list — add one above, or nobody can offer a tip.

invites.title: The guest list
invites.lead: {members, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} can send you models, and {open, plural, one {# invite is} other {# invites are}} still outstanding. Links expire after {days} days and work exactly once.
invites.none: Nobody yet. The office is very quiet.

guests.inviteLead: They get a link that works once and expires in a week. There is no other way in.
guests.name: Name (optional)
guests.emailed: Sent · {email} has been emailed a link
guests.suspendedHelp: {name} cannot sign in. Restoring lets them back in with the password or passkey they already had — nothing was deleted.
guests.revokeHelp: Signs {name} out everywhere and refuses any new sign-in. Their tickets, comments and history stay exactly as they are, and you can restore access at any time. Recorded in the audit log.
guests.resetHelp: Mints a single-use link that lets {name} pick a new password, valid {minutes} minutes. It does not sign anyone in, it signs {name} out everywhere, and it is recorded in the audit log.
guests.resetSent: Sent to {email}. The link is inside the message and nowhere else — not even here.
guests.handOverHelp: Nobody was emailed — there is no mail server configured. Send this to them however you normally would.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.lead: Every action that changes who can get in, or what happens to someone’s model. Nothing here is ever edited or removed.
audit.refusalsToday: {count, plural, one {# refusal in the last day} other {# refusals in the last day}}
audit.worthALook: — worth a look if that is more than you expect.
audit.showingOfMore: Showing the most recent {count} of more.

refusals.title: Anything being refused
refusals.none: Nothing was turned away. That is the expected reading — this panel is here for the week it is not.

stages.title: Where the work is sitting
stages.usuallyHelp: Usually is the median this stage has taken, measured off the trail. A queue that is deep but quick is not the same problem as one that is shallow and slow.

mix.kicker: {count, plural, one {# request in all} other {# requests in all}}
mix.title: What gets asked for

settings.title: House rules
settings.lead: The few things about this instance you can change without touching the server. A save is in effect from the next request — no restart. Anything set in the environment wins, and is shown here locked with the variable that sets it.
settings.importSourcesHelp: Lets a request start from a model’s page instead of an upload. The server then fetches the file itself, so it needs outbound HTTPS to that site.
settings.senderNameHelp: The name invitations and reset links arrive from. The address stays in MAIL_FROM.
settings.noTransportYet: — once there is a transport; there is none yet.
settings.reauth: Asks for your password or passkey again if you signed in more than five minutes ago.
settings.allFromEnv: Everything here is set by the environment.

env.title: Set in the environment
env.lead: Read-only. These are decided where the app is started, in .env.docker, and change with a restart.
env.signInHow: Username and password · passkeys · API bearer tokens
env.breachOff: Off — passwords are not checked against known breaches
env.breachOn: On — passwords in a known breach are refused
env.passkeyNameWhy: Stays in the environment: the passkey library reads it once, when the app starts, and a passkey keeps the name it was made with.

mailKind.none: Not configured — invitation and reset links are shown to you to hand over

proxy.none: Not trusted — the audit trail records no address

ticket.flagReason: What is wrong with the model
ticket.declineConfirm: Decline this one? It cannot be undone.

account.roleOwner: Owns the printer, sees every ticket
account.roleMember: Invited by {owner} · sees only their own tickets
account.listOwner: Everything the group has sent you
account.emptyOwner: Nobody has sent you anything yet.
account.declinedToo: Declined orders are listed here too — the rail only carries what is still moving.
